liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lost Sailor** (2 reviews): The jam from Drums into Lost Sailor is unusual, since the song normally begins from a complete stop; Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance has a seeking quality, then soars and lands in Comes a Time [11][16]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Let It Grow one of the best of 1980, a sizzling version [6]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): The Eyes jam into Space gains momentum and takes off, with intricate playing [16]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 other source): Listed as the encore [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Other One Jam**: back after 268 archived shows (1394 days) [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-29.152534.aud.gems.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 163 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer considers this audience recording about as good as audience recordings get; A tape flip during Drums/Space was handled well with a crossfade, so very little music was lost [1][14]
- **gd1980-05-29.152539.aud.gems.flac1648**: audience recording; 24 songs; 163 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Lovely audience recording, except that the drums are barely audible [15]
- **gd80-05-29.aud.vernon.14836.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 150 min; rated 2.5/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Microphone placement and crowd levels are good, but warble suggests a second-generation or heavily played source [8]
- **gd80-05-29.pset1-set2.nak300.braveman.25993.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 14 songs; 102 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Low-generation audience tape with very clean sound, though the recording is only partial; Reviewer finds the sound poor and says songs are missing from this copy [6][7]
- **gd1980-05-29.152540.sbd.s2.patched.gems.flac1644**: soundboard; 13 songs; 92 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Patched soundboard from partial source material; reviewer hopes the complete soundboard of the show eventually turns up [13]

## Around the show

- Inside, the reviewer found it one of the smallest venues they had seen the band play [9]
- Reviewer ranks Seattle's Let It Grow alongside it, and suggests the last Nassau night and Penn State as similar [6]
- Some jams are short, as in early and mid 1980, but the show builds in strength as it goes [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-29.152534.aud.gems.flac2496**: taped by ANON; transferred by Speed Correction by Jason Chastain Critical Listening and Track FLAC, Pack by Steven Gravel Mastering by Jamie Waddell; source: Roughly 10th row FOB master audience tapes from an Anonymous Benefactor, actual gear lost to the fog of memory, [1]. Also: Uploader describes this as the first quality recording of the show; Shared at shnflac.net in May 2021, then broadcast on KXCI Tucson's Dead Air on May 30, 2021 [1]
- **gd1980-05-29.152539.aud.gems.flac1648**: taped by ANON; transferred by Speed Correction by Jason Chastain Critical Listening and Track FLAC, Pack by Steven Gravel Mastering by Jamie Waddell; source: Roughly 10th row FOB master audience tapes from an Anonymous Benefactor, actual gear lost to the fog of memory, [2]
- **gd80-05-29.aud.vernon.14836.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: Audience-recording chain: A:C:C:D, then CDR via David Minches, with shn encoding by Matt Vernon [3]
- **gd80-05-29.pset1-set2.nak300.braveman.25993.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by jbraveman; source: Audience Recording: Nak 300 [4]
- **gd1980-05-29.152540.sbd.s2.patched.gems.flac1644**: source: Patched soundboard [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 5/29/1980 Des Moines IA Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/dead_pass_80529.html) [18]
